note: Upstream sources the personal-voice engine is built from, pinned to exact commits, plus the wheels built from them. The repositories are NOT vendored: they are third-party MIT projects and copying them would make Videofy responsible for code it does not maintain. The wheels are built locally and identified by hash rather than committed.

sources.role: Tone-colour converter: extracts a speaker representation and repaints base-speaker audio with it.
sources.installedWithReason: Upstream metadata requires faster-whisper==0.9.0 (and through it an old PyAV that fails to build from source), whisper-timestamped and a pinned gradio — all for the se_extractor/Whisper path Videofy never calls. Proved by scripts/openvoice-runtime-graph.py, which exercises the real path and reports that none of them are imported. Its genuine runtime need, wavmark, is installed explicitly.

sources.role: Base speakers. Delivery — accent, rhythm, expressiveness — comes from here rather than from the enrolled voice.

deliberateExclusions.reason: Required by upstream OpenVoice metadata for se_extractor, which this service does not use. Never imported by the executed path.
Installs an EMPTY Japanese dictionary directory that mecab then prefers over the bundled unidic-lite, breaking French synthesis at import time. Videofy synthesises no Japanese.

additionalRuntimeRequirements.reason: ToneColorConverter imports it at construction. The service watermarks every generated clip, so this is genuinely required and was skipped by --no-deps.
librosa 0.9.1 imports pkg_resources, which newer setuptools no longer provides.

rebuild: python scripts/openvoice-runtime-graph.py     # must import none of the excluded packages

isolationProof.result: converter produced audio with the source checkouts unavailable
